chunks: Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim asked him about a man who prayed, then remembered that he had added an extra sajdah.
He said: “He does not repeat his salat because of one sajdah, but he repeats it because of one rak‘ah.”
And ʿĀmir ibn Judhāʿah narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:
“If the first two rak‘ahs are sound, the salat is sound.”
ai.seo_question: Does adding an extra sajdah or rak‘ah require repeating the prayer?
ai.summary: These narrations address rulings of forgetfulness in salat. They distinguish between adding a sajdah and adding a full rak‘ah, and they emphasize the importance of the soundness of the first two rak‘ahs in the validity of the prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1009 - Mansour ibn Hazim asked Imam (as) about a person who prayed and then remembered that he had added an extra prostration.
Imam (as) said: "He does not need to repeat his prayer due to the extra prostration, but he must repeat it from the point of the ruku' (bowing)”.

1010 - وَ رَوَى عَامِرُ بْنُ جُذَاعَةَ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا سَلِمَتِ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَانِ سَلِمَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ.
Hadith.1010 - Amir ibn Jadh'ah narrated from Imam (as) that He said:
"If the first two rak'ahs are correct, the whole prayer is correct”.
